claims.claim: Barely used, bought new last year. No fault at all, the motor was never opened. Receipt and warranty card available.

risks.risk: Microwave may not heat properly (magnetron/transformer issue) even if it looks intact.
risks.proof: A short video of it heating a cup of water (show start time and that it boils/strongly heats).
risks.if_unproven: Price it as not proven working (worst case: needs repair / not reliable).

risks.risk: Door seal/hinges may be faulty, causing leakage or failure to start.
risks.proof: Photo/clip of the door seal area + a test showing it starts reliably with the door closed.
risks.if_unproven: Price it as potential door/starting issue until tested.

risks.risk: Turntable/roller ring may be missing or not functioning.
risks.proof: Photo of the inside cavity showing turntable/roller set, plus a clip of it rotating while heating.
risks.if_unproven: Price it as missing/unknown accessories (worst case: not included).

risks.risk: Exact brand/model and wattage are unclear, which affects value and comparables.
risks.proof: Clear photo of the rating plate (back/bottom) showing brand, model, and wattage.
risks.if_unproven: Price it at the lowest likely spec for a generic countertop microwave.

risks.risk: Warranty/receipt may not be available or may not be transferable/valid.
risks.proof: Photos of the receipt and warranty card (with dates and serial/model matching the unit).
risks.if_unproven: Price it as no usable warranty.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the rating plate (back or bottom) showing brand, model, and wattage.
Video of the microwave running: heat a cup of water and show it starting and heating (ideally boiling).
Photo of the inside cavity showing turntable/roller set (and confirm included accessories).
Photos of receipt and warranty card with matching model/serial.
response.reason: The photo confirms it is a countertop microwave oven, but the brand/model and wattage are not readable and there is no power-on test. Seller claims of working condition and warranty cannot be verified remotely, so pricing would be guesswork without the key proof.
